result.summary: Extracts logic for nine P2P message types out of the monolithic `PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage()` into dedicated private member functions in `src/net_processing.cpp`. Each message handler is extracted in its own move-only commit, followed by a final cleanup commit normalizing formatting and minor control flow in the extracted helpers.
result.problem: `PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage()` is an oversized (~1,000-line) function processing many P2P message types inline, making navigation, scoping, and review in `net_processing` difficult.
evidence: Continues the extraction pattern of previously merged commits fa5ab0220e (`ProcessPong()`) and fa55723b8f (`ProcessAddrs()`), as suggested in PR #34588 review comments.
result.scope_notes: Large move-only refactoring (+1082/-1033) confined to `src/net_processing.cpp`, divided into nine per-message extraction commits designed to be reviewed with `--color-moved=dimmed-zebra --color-moved-ws=ignore-all-space`, followed by one formatting cleanup commit.
result.changed_since_previous: Added a tenth commit that cleans up formatting, replaces `break` statements with `return` in `ProcessSendTxRcncl()`, and simplifies the `send_getaddr` conditional in `ProcessVersion()`.
result.card: Extracts handling logic for nine P2P message types out of `PeerManagerImpl::ProcessMessage()` in `src/net_processing.cpp` into dedicated helper functions across nine move-only commits and one cleanup commit. The function is an oversized monolith handling many message types inline, making navigation and code maintenance in `net_processing` cumbersome. The author notes this continues previously merged cleanup work splitting up the ~1,000-line function. It makes no intentional functional changes aside from a function name in one debug log.

risk.why: A subtle logic error or unintended control-flow difference introduced while extracting P2P message handlers could cause peer disconnections, protocol violations, or remote processing stalls.
